narrative.summary: Mozambique has no AI law. Since April 2026 a decree (Decree 14/2026) has set up a National Artificial Intelligence Commission, with the national ICT institute (INTIC) as its secretariat. The 2024 Science, Technology and Innovation Policy and the Government Five-Year Programme 2025-2029 commit to an ethics-aligned national AI strategy and AI ethics principles, and the draft National AI Strategy 2026-2031 completed public consultation in September 2026 but has not been adopted. A draft digital transformation strategy is also in consultation.
lead_institutions: Instituto Nacional de Tecnologias de Informação e Comunicação (INTIC)
Ministry of Communications and Digital Transformation
narrative.review_notes: This review was first completed on 12 October 2026 and redone in a longer pass on 13 October 2026, covering official gazette copies hosted by the ICT institute, Parliament, the government, each ministry and each sector regulator. Not yet verified from the official text: material on the official gazette's own website and of most line ministries. Two drafts whose publication dates are not stated by the issuer (a cybersecurity strategy and a data governance policy) were moved to leads, together with the central bank's announced AI policy and the pending data protection bill.

instruments.official_title: Proposta da Estratégia Nacional de Inteligência Artificial de Moçambique (ENIA) 2026–2031
instruments.english_title: Proposal for the National Artificial Intelligence Strategy of Mozambique (ENIA) 2026–2031
instruments.issuing_authority: National Institute of Information and Communication Technologies (INTIC), for the Government of Mozambique
instruments.current_status: Not adopted. INTIC published the first version of the proposal for public consultation on 5 May 2026; the consultation page and the 'Propostas de instrumentos legais' hub now link 'Proposta (Draft 6) da ENIA' (the hub also lists 'Draft 2') and state that contributions were due by 4 September (2026). As of 13 October 2026 no adopting Council of Ministers resolution was found; the draft's preface is still a placeholder. The draft cites Decree 14/2026 (CNIA) as the national AI coordination body.
instruments.summary: Draft national AI strategy for 2026-2031, built around six pillars (science, infrastructure and ecosystem; social applications and human development; digital economy and industry; security, resilience and environmental sustainability; fundamental rights, information and democracy; AI governance, trust and supervision), with an action plan and budget annex. It proposes a national AI governance model centred on the National AI Commission (CNIA) with INTIC as ICT regulator and executive secretariat, a National AI Governance and Trust Framework (QNGC-IA), a national risk classification for AI systems, national and sectoral AI regulatory sandboxes, a national AI testing and audit centre, an AI observatory and a future Mozambican AI law.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: First national AI strategy, in public consultation; sets out the planned institutional and regulatory model for AI.
instruments.publisher_name: National Institute of Information and Communication Technologies

instruments.current_status: Adopted and in force: computed from art. 3 (in force from the date of publication) and publication in Boletim da República I Série n.º 142 on 2024-07-23. Copy of the gazette issue hosted by INTIC (a state body) on its 'Políticas e Estratégias' page; the file name mislabels it as the Five-Year Government Programme. The draft ENIA (2026) cites it as its basis.
instruments.summary: Council of Ministers resolution (approved 21 May 2024, published in Boletim da República I Série n.º 142 of 23 July 2024) adopting the Science, Technology and Innovation Policy (PCTI) and its implementation strategy, revoking Resolution 23/2003. Under the pillar on capacity to use frontier and emerging technologies, strategic intervention iv is the development of a national AI strategy aligned with ethics, which the Government must ensure covers safety, transparency, credibility and the ethical use of AI; it also calls for a national Fourth Industrial Revolution strategy.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: The adopted policy mandate for a national AI strategy; the draft ENIA cites it as its basis.

instruments.summary: Draft national digital transformation strategy prepared by the Ministry of Communications and Digital Transformation with ITU technical assistance, structured around five transformative changes (connected, served, productive, empowered, protected) and six implementation pillars. Its guiding objectives include using AI and emerging technologies responsibly to strengthen service delivery, governance, productivity, innovation and resilience, and it sets a target of at least 5,000 professionals trained in AI, data science and cybersecurity.

instruments.official_title: Decreto n.º 14/2026, de 17 de Abril, que cria a Comissão Nacional de Inteligência Artificial, abreviadamente designada por CNIA
instruments.english_title: Decree No. 14/2026 of 17 April creating the National Commission for Artificial Intelligence (CNIA)
instruments.current_status: In force: computed from art. 12 (in force on the date of publication) and publication in Boletim da República I Série n.º 72 on 2026-04-17. Approved by the Council of Ministers on 10 March 2026 (7th ordinary session). Art. 11 required the CNIA to approve its internal rules within 30 days of publication; those rules were not found online. The draft ENIA's text also calls it 'Resolução n.º 14/2026'; the gazette confirms it is a decree.
instruments.summary: Council of Ministers decree creating the National Commission for Artificial Intelligence (CNIA), a consultative and technical advisory body to the Government on AI, subordinate to the Council of Ministers, with a subcommission for defence and security. The CNIA advises on AI strategy taking ethics and security into account, gives opinions on AI policies, strategies and proposed legal and regulatory instruments, advises on ethical, legal and security issues, impact studies and international standards, and must publish activity reports and opinions every six months. It is chaired by the ICT minister (vice-chairs: defence and education ministers), brings in ministries, regulators (ICT, communications, financial sector, health research), the Supreme Court, prosecution service, private sector and civil society, and the ICT regulatory authority (INTIC) is its executive secretariat, charged among other things with coordinating implementation of the National AI Strategy.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Founding instrument of Mozambique's national AI body; the institutional anchor for the draft ENIA's governance model.

instruments.summary: Assembly of the Republic resolution approving the Government's five-year programme for 2025-2029, the main medium-term planning instrument derived from the National Development Strategy 2025-2044. In the operational matrix of the Scientific Research, Technology and Innovation programme, strategic action 18 commits the Government to develop guiding principles for the use of AI aligned with a regulatory framework for AI ethics, based on the UNESCO Recommendation on the Ethics of AI, measured by the number of AI guiding instruments produced and of public awareness events on AI.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Adopted government programme committing to AI ethics guiding principles for 2025-2029; cited by the draft ENIA as introducing AI as a strategic technology for state modernisation.

coverage_audit.no_material_found_note: Mozambique's gazette copies, parliament, the information and communications technology regulator, each ministry and sector regulator were searched. Records include Decree 14/2026 and the Government Programme approved by Resolution 17/2025, which includes AI ethics principles; there is no data protection law, and there was no material for procurement, cybersecurity, data and privacy, transparency, standards, indices, specific sectors, generative AI or international instruments. The central bank's AI policy and draft AI rules, the personal data protection bill and ministry AI documents remain to be checked.
coverage_audit.technical_note:
Coverage note (original): Technical review notes: thin pass 2026-10-13 (second, longer deep review: up to 45 minutes, one agent, national level only, PROTOCOL §6; every existing record re-checked; each ministry and sector regulator searched one by one). Thin pass 2026-10-13: 5 existing records re-checked. i-5c0a0045022c URL fixed (encoding of 'É'; new source id, old source orphaned) and effective_date 2024-07-23 computed from art. 3 (in force on publication). i-a5a49690f4da (draft cybersecurity strategy, date from upload path) and i-4e83bd05d27b (draft data governance policy, no stated date) dropped to leads (PROTOCOL §4). Added Decree 14/2026 (CNIA; in force 2026-04-17 per art. 12; promoted from lead) and Resolution 17/2025 approving the Government Programme 2025-2029 (action 18: AI ethics principles). About 19 BR issues hosted by INTIC read; Laws 13/2026 and 14/2026 (BR 123, 1 Jul 2026), Decrees 71/2025, 72/2025, 59/2023 (am. 44/2025), Law 3/2017: no AI. Not reached: imprensanac.gov.mz, mctes, mec/mined, misau, mjcr, mdn, mef (403), at, mitess, agricultura, arc, bvm, innoq, inage. WebFetch could not read the CNIA PDF text or the Programme PDF (>10 MB); curl read both. Convention 108: not a party. Units covered: Law: Imprensa Nacional / Boletim da República site unreachable again (curl connection reset/502, WebFetch 503), so its own search could not be used; instead every Boletim da República copy hosted by INTIC (legislation 'Sectorial' page and 'Políticas e Estratégias' page, 14+5 issues) was read. Data centre and cloud regulations (Decrees 71 and 72/2025), digital platforms regulation (Decree 59/2023 as amended by 44/2025), Electronic Transactions Law 3/2017, 2021 Cyber Security Policy: no AI provisions (2021 policy mentions AI only in context).
